text:
Buffalo arrives at the end of a four-game road trip (2-0-1 so far) fresh off a 7-6 comeback in Anaheim, where the Sabres erased a two-goal deficit, Tage Thompson scored three times and Roger McQueen got his first NHL goal. They're missing Justin Danforth, Konsta Helenius and Jiri Kulich. Los Angeles is in game two of a six-game home stand after Quinton Byfield won it in overtime against Ottawa, 6-5. The Kings are without Mats Zuccarello, who has 54 points last season and is out until about Nov. 10. Artemi Panarin has taken his spot beside Haula and Laferriere, and Erik Gustafsson has moved onto the first power-play unit.

Our numbers see little between them: Buffalo has 52% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five, Los Angeles 48%, and our model projects 3.18 to 2.97 for the Sabres. The special-teams matchup to watch is the Kings' power play, which creates 0.82 expected goals a game, against a Buffalo penalty kill that allows 0.82. Projected goalies: Colten Ellis is +1.1 goals saved above expected this season for Buffalo, while Darcy Kuemper is at -3.7 for Los Angeles, and -6.8 last season.

Thompson is our model's top Sabre at 37% to score, and he leads the power play. For the Kings, Panarin has a 74% chance at a point, and Adrian Kempe (37% to score) has gone five games without a goal on 2.8 expected goals.
